column1: # Dataset: Business Survivability Scores by Neighborhood - San Antonio (2026)
# Description: Predicted probability (0-100%) that a business type survives 2+ years at neighborhood level in San Antonio
# Scores are based on 100+ location factors and 570
column2: 000+ real business outcomes across 24 US metros

column1: # Columns: city = Metro slug (for example philadelphia).; neighborhood = Neighborhood slug inside the metro; the row's place.; business_subtype = Business type slug (110 types
column2: for example italian-restaurant); the row's business.; business_type_lookup = The broader category the subtype belongs to (restaurant
column5: health).; avg_survivability_score = The headline number: the projected chance
column7: that this business type lasts two or more years at a typical address in this neighborhood. Use this column to answer 'where should I open X'.; max_survivability_score = Best address in the neighborhood for this business type
column8: 0 to 100.; the rest are in the README

column2: Where should I open a given business in this metro? Filter business_subtype to the type (for example italian-restaurant)
column4: read the top rows: those neighborhoods are where that business is projected to last two or more years most often. neighborhood_rank_for_business_subtype gives the same order as a number.

column2: What should I open in a given neighborhood? Filter neighborhood to the place
column3: sort by business_subtype_rank_for_neighborhood ascending (or avg_survivability_score descending): the top rows are the business types most likely to last there.

column2: How do two neighborhoods compare for the same business? Filter business_subtype to the type and neighborhood to the two places; compare avg_survivability_score
column3: then max and min for the best and worst address in each. A gap of 5 points or more is material; the confidence bounds say how firm it is.
